key_insight: Detonation-sprayed AlCuFe quasicrystalline coatings form a stable, oxidation-resistant barrier at 450°C by slowly transforming from icosahedral QC to multi-phase approximants while maintaining and even increasing hardness.
engineering_relevance: The coating offers a promising long-term protective layer for TC4 titanium alloys in high-temperature oxidizing environments, helping preserve surface integrity and mechanical performance.
method: Fabricated AlCuFe QC coatings by detonation spraying (DS).
Aged the coatings in air at 450°C for up to 250 h.
Tracked oxidation kinetics, phase evolution, and microhardness over time.
evidence_signal: The oxidation followed a parabolic law with kp = 1.83 × 10^-2 mg^2·cm^-4·h^-1, while microhardness rose from 491 HV0.2 to 665.2 HV0.2 after 250 h.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated at a single test temperature and atmosphere, so broader service conditions and coating-substrate durability still need validation.
paper_title: High-temperature oxidation kinetics and microstructural evolution of detonation-sprayed AlCuFe quasicrystalline coatings
